Πέντε ερωτήματα που βοηθούν να δείτε πέρα από τις αίθουσες και τα προγράμματα, είτε ψάχνετε Νηπιαγωγείο είτε σκέφτεστε την Α΄ Δημοτικού.
        Ένας νεκρός και τρεις τραυματίες από δύο περιστατικά πυροβολισμών σε πανεπιστήμιο στη Βόρεια Καρολίνα 
    
Συνελήφθη 20χρονος για την πρώτη επίθεση στο Πανεπιστήμιο Γουίνστον-Σέιλεμ - Οι Αρχές ερευνούν εάν συνδέονται τα δύο περιστατικά
Ένας 19χρονος έχασε τη ζωή του και τουλάχιστον τρία άτομα τραυματίστηκαν σε δύο περιστατικά πυροβολισμών που σημειώθηκαν με διαφορά μικρότερη της μίας ώρας στο Πολιτειακό Πανεπιστήμιο Γουίνστον-Σέιλεμ, στη Βόρεια Καρολίνα των ΗΠΑ, κατά τη διάρκεια των εορταστικών εκδηλώσεων για την επιστροφή των αποφοίτων (homecoming). Για την πρώτη επίθεση συνελήφθη ένας 20χρονος, ο οποίος δεν είναι φοιτητής του πανεπιστημίου, ενώ οι αστυνομικές Αρχές εξετάζουν εάν τα δύο περιστατικά σχετίζονται μεταξύ τους.
Το πρώτο περιστατικό σημειώθηκε περίπου στις 21:45 το βράδυ του Σαββάτου (04:45 τα ξημερώματα της Κυριακής, ώρα Ελλάδας), όταν αστυνομικοί που βρίσκονταν στην πανεπιστημιούπολη για την ασφάλεια των εκδηλώσεων άκουσαν πυροβολισμούς.
Σπεύδοντας στο σημείο, εντόπισαν έναν 19χρονο άνδρα με τραύμα από σφαίρα. Παρά τις προσπάθειές τους να του προσφέρουν τις πρώτες βοήθειες, ο νεαρός υπέκυψε στα τραύματά του επί τόπου.
Από το ίδιο περιστατικό τραυματίστηκε και μία 22χρονη γυναίκα, η οποία μεταφέρθηκε σε νοσοκομείο με τραύμα που, σύμφωνα με τις Αρχές, φαινόταν να έχει προκληθεί από πυροβολισμό. Αφού δέχθηκε ιατρική φροντίδα, πήρε εξιτήριο.
Συνελήφθη 20χρονος για ανθρωποκτονία
Όπως ανακοίνωσε σε συνέντευξη Τύπου ο βοηθός αρχηγού της Αστυνομίας, Τζέισον Σουέιμ, οι έρευνες οδήγησαν στον εντοπισμό και τη σύλληψη του 20χρονου Ζιγέρ Σπινκς την Κυριακή.
Σε βάρος του απαγγέλθηκαν κατηγορίες για ανθρωποκτονία, επίθεση με φονικό όπλο και κατοχή πυροβόλου όπλου σε εκπαιδευτικό ίδρυμα. Ο νεαρός κρατείται χωρίς δυνατότητα αποφυλάκισης με εγγύηση.
Σύμφωνα με την Αστυνομία, οι πυροβολισμοί προκλήθηκαν έπειτα από διαπληκτισμό ανάμεσα σε δύο ομάδες ατόμων. Οι Αρχές διευκρίνισαν ότι ο συλληφθείς δεν φοιτούσε στο πανεπιστήμιο.
Δεύτερο περιστατικό με δύο τραυματίες μέσα σε λιγότερο από μία ώρα
Πριν συμπληρωθεί μία ώρα από την πρώτη επίθεση, σημειώθηκε δεύτερο περιστατικό πυροβολισμών στην ίδια πανεπιστημιούπολη.
Αστυνομικοί που άκουσαν και πάλι πυροβολισμούς κινητοποιήθηκαν άμεσα. Σύμφωνα με τον Τζέισον Σουέιμ, η ανταλλαγή πυρών σημειώθηκε έπειτα από συμπλοκή, με αποτέλεσμα να τραυματιστούν δύο άνθρωποι.
Για τη δεύτερη υπόθεση δεν έχουν πραγματοποιηθεί συλλήψεις, ενώ οι ερευνητές προσπαθούν να διαπιστώσουν εάν υπάρχει σύνδεση ανάμεσα στα δύο περιστατικά.
«Θα εντοπίσουμε όλους όσοι ευθύνονται»
Ο αρχηγός της Αστυνομίας του Γουίνστον-Σέιλεμ, Γουίλιαμ Πεν Τζούνιορ, διαβεβαίωσε κατά τη διάρκεια συνέντευξης Τύπου ότι οι Αρχές θα εντοπίσουν όλους όσοι εμπλέκονται στα βίαια επεισόδια.
«Είναι σημαντικό η ευθύνη γι' αυτά τα τραγικά γεγονότα να αποδοθεί στους σωστούς ανθρώπους, δηλαδή σε εκείνους που διέπραξαν αυτές τις πράξεις», δήλωσε.
Παράλληλα, κάλεσε τους πολίτες να αποφύγουν τις αλληλοκατηγορίες και την απόδοση ευθυνών προτού ολοκληρωθεί η αστυνομική έρευνα.
Την ίδια ώρα, στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης, μέλη της τοπικής κοινότητας εξέφραζαν τα συλλυπητήριά τους και απηύθυναν εκκλήσεις για προσευχές.
Αυξημένα μέτρα ασφαλείας και ψυχολογική υποστήριξη στους φοιτητές
Η πρύτανης του Πανεπιστημίου Γουίνστον-Σέιλεμ, Μπονίτα Τζ. Μπράουν, χαρακτήρισε τα περιστατικά «παράλογη βία», διαβεβαιώνοντας τους φοιτητές, το διδακτικό προσωπικό και τους γονείς ότι η πανεπιστημιούπολη είναι ασφαλής.
Όπως ανακοίνωσε, πρόσθετες αστυνομικές δυνάμεις θα παραμείνουν στον χώρο για όσο διάστημα συνεχίζονται οι έρευνες.
Παράλληλα, το πανεπιστήμιο προσφέρει υπηρεσίες ψυχολογικής υποστήριξης σε όσους έχουν ανάγκη μετά τα βίαια γεγονότα.
«Αναγνωρίζουμε επίσης την ανησυχία και το άγχος που έχουν προκαλέσει αυτά τα περιστατικά στους φοιτητές, στους γονείς, στις οικογένειες και στην ευρύτερη κοινότητά μας», ανέφερε η Μπράουν.
«Αντιμετωπίζουμε με σοβαρότητα την ευθύνη μας για την ασφάλεια της πανεπιστημιούπολης», πρόσθεσε.
Στο ίδιο μήκος κύματος κινήθηκε και ο σερίφης της κομητείας Φόρσαϊθ, Μπόμπι Κίμπρο Τζούνιορ, ο οποίος ζήτησε από την τοπική κοινωνία να παραμείνει ενωμένη.
«Αυτή τη στιγμή, η κοινότητα χρειάζεται τις προσευχές σας. Η κοινότητα έχει ανάγκη να σταθούμε όλοι μαζί», δήλωσε κατά τη συνέντευξη Τύπου.

sources.news_title: Man arrested after deadly shooting at Winston-Salem State University
sources.text:
Man arrested after deadly shooting at Winston-Salem State University during homecoming weekend
Police said there were two separate shootings on campus on Saturday night
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Join today
Already a member? Log in
A 20-year-old man is being held without bond on murder and firearms charges after a shooting at a historically Black university in North Carolina left one person dead and at least one other person injured.
The shooting took place at Winston-Salem State University during homecoming weekend, and police said detectives had determined it was an isolated incident.
Ziyaire Spinks, 20, faces charges of murder and possession of a firearm on educational property, according to Assistant Police Chief Jason Swaim of the Winston-Salem Police Department.
Swaim said the circumstances surrounding the shooting were still under investigation.
Officers were alerted by gunshots at around 9.45pm on Saturday and responded to the campus, Swaim said.
They found a 19-year-old man with a gunshot wound, but life-saving measures were unsuccessful.
A 22-year-old woman found at the scene appeared to have a gunshot wound as well. She was taken to a hospital, where she was treated and later released.
Police had said during an early morning news conference that two separate shootings occurred on campus on Saturday night. No details about the second shooting have been shared.
University officials canceled the remainder of the homecoming activities. Instead, they said a local church had planned to lead a call for prayers in support of the community.
Chancellor Bonita J. Brown issued a statement on Sunday morning, calling the shootings “senseless violence.”
She assured students, faculty and parents that the campus was secure and that additional law enforcement would remain while the investigation continues. The school was offering counseling for anyone in need.
“We also recognize the concern and anxiety these events have created among our students, parents, families and broader community,” Brown said. “We take our responsibility for campus safety seriously and remain committed to the well-being of everyone who is part of our university community.”

sources.news_title: 1 dead, 3 others injured following two separate shootings at university in NC
sources.text:
1 dead, 3 others injured following two separate shootings at Winston-Salem State University
The Winston-Salem Police Department said one person has died and three others were shot following two separate shooting incidents on Winston-Salem State University's campus Saturday.
The Winston-Salem Police Department held a news conference early Sunday morning around 1:45 a.m. to give an update.
“Our condolences go out to the families, to the friends, and anyone who witnessed this,” officials said.
Police said they received a call around 9:45 p.m. Saturday night about a shooting. Police have not released any information concerning the circumstances around both shootings or the conditions of the victims at this time.
WXII 12 News asked if someone was arrested but they said they didn’t have any information.
As of 1:25 a.m. Sunday, police were allowing students to walk to their dorms on campus. Police said the campus was placed on lockdown but it has since been lifted.
Law enforcement officials said extra officers will be on and around campus in the coming days.
The investigation is ongoing at this time.
Winston-Salem State University Chancellor releases statement
Winston-Salem State University Chancellor Bonita J. Brown released the following statement:
"Dear Ramily,
Homecoming is a time we come together to celebrate connections and shared experiences. Today, however, we find ourselves coming together under heartbreaking circumstances.
On Saturday, Nov. 7, two separate shootings occurred on our campus, resulting in the loss of one life and injuries to three others. This senseless violence has shaken our university community, and our hearts are heavy.
First and foremost, I extend my deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of the individual who lost their life. Our thoughts and prayers are also with those who were injured, and we wish them a full recovery.
I recognize that members of our university community may have witnessed or experienced things that no one should have to endure. I understand the fear, grief and uncertainty that many of you may be feeling. Please know you are not alone. Students can access counseling services at (336) 750-3270 or through Togetherall. In-person counseling will also be available Sunday, Nov. 8, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and Monday, Nov. 9, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. in DJR100 and DJR205. Faculty and staff can access free, confidential support 24/7 through the ComPsych Employee Assistance Program (EAP) by calling 866-922-5712 or visiting https://bit.ly/3UHW5ND.
I want to reassure our students, parents, alumni and the entire university community that our campus is secure, with no active threat at this time, as confirmed by the Winston-Salem Police Department. Additional law enforcement personnel remain on campus as the investigations continue.
We are grateful to WSSU Police and Public Safety, the Winston-Salem Police Department and the Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office for their response and continued efforts to protect our campus community. We remain committed to working closely with authorities as they investigate both incidents.
We also recognize the concern and anxiety these events have created among our students, parents, families and broader community. We take our responsibility for campus safety seriously and remain committed to the well-being of everyone who is part of our university community.
In light of these tragic incidents, we have canceled today's remaining Homecoming activities, including the Fourth Quarter event and WSSU's participation in WSSU Day at Emmanuel Baptist Church. We are grateful that the church will instead lead a Call to Prayer in support of our university community.
Please continue to follow law enforcement instructions and avoid any areas that remain restricted. As a reminder, we encourage all members of the campus community to continue practicing everyday safety measures, including being aware of their surroundings, using well-lit routes, keeping residence halls secure by using your own authorized access and not allowing unauthorized individuals to enter behind you, and reporting suspicious activity or safety concerns to WSSU Police and Public Safety by calling (336) 750-2911 or through the Rave Guardian app.
Throughout our history, Winston-Salem State University has faced challenges, but we have always found strength in one another. That is what it means to be part of the Ramily and to be Ram strong. As we move forward, I ask that you continue to keep the families and all those affected in the broader Winston-Salem community in your thoughts and prayers. Let us remain united in our commitment to the university we love."
Keep up with what's happening around our area by downloading the WYFF News 4 app on the App Store or Google Play.

sources.text:
Two Shootings at NC College Leave 1 Dead, 3 Injured
|                          By Newser Editors and Wire Services                                                                                                            Posted Nov 8, 2026  8:55 AM CST                                                       | 
Two separate shootings during homecoming weekend at a college in North Carolina have left one person dead and three injured, police said Sunday. Assistant Police Chief Jason Swaim of the Winston-Salem Police Department said both shootings occurred Saturday on the campus of Winston-Salem State University but that it was too early to tell whether they were connected. No details were provided on the victims, and it appears that no arrests have been made.
"At this point, the investigation is still very early in its preliminary stages," Swaim said at a press conference early Sunday. Authorities, however, said the campus of the historically Black college is safe. The shooting follows other college-related shootings in previous weeks in Tallahassee, Florida, and in Birmingham, Alabama.

sources.news_title: 1 killed and 3 wounded in shootings on Winston-Salem State University campus
sources.text:
Authorities have arrested a man in connection with one of two shootings on Winston-Salem State University’s campus that killed a person and wounded three other people Saturday.
Ziyaire Antonyo Spinks, 20, was arrested in connection with a shooting that killed Peyton Izaia Patterson, 19, Winston-Salem police said in a statement Sunday. Spinks was charged with murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury and felony possession of a firearm on an educational campus.
Officers who responded after they heard shots fired found Patterson with a gunshot wound. The officers and emergency medical services attempted lifesaving measures, police said, but he did not survive.
The shooting injured Alyssa Janae Ellerbee, 19, who was treated at a hospital and later released, police said.
Police have determined the shooting to be an isolated incident, not connected to a separate shooting that also occurred on campus Saturday night.
Spinks is being held without bond, according to police.
Court records show he has two previous court cases pending in North Carolina.
He has a pending case in Randolph County involving charges of carrying a concealed weapon and marijuana possession from an arrest in March. The lawyer representing him in the March case told NBC News on Sunday that he was unaware of the new charges in Winston-Salem, in Forsyth County.
Spinks was indicted in October on charges of felony conspiracy to commit robbery and robbery with a dangerous weapon in Guilford County. The incident is alleged to have occurred last year, but the indictment was filed on Oct. 5, according to court records.
The attorney representing him in Guilford County did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The shooting stemmed from an altercation between two groups, according to Jason Swaim, assistant chief of the Winston-Salem police Field Services Bureau. An additional person, Cequon Warren Brower, 18, was arrested in connection with fighting.
“One thing I’ll add about the homicide on campus — because I know this has been a question — is that the arrestee that’s been charged with murder, Mr. Spinks, he was not a student of Winston-Salem State University, and neither was Cequon Brower,” Swaim told reporters Sunday.
That shooting occurred at 9:46 p.m., and another shooting was reported on campus at 10:22 p.m., Swaim said.
Officers found two people with gunshot wounds. A vehicle related to that incident was identified and later stopped by West Side police officers. No arrests had been made in that case Sunday afternoon, Swaim said.
Saturday was homecoming game day at the historically Black university, with the WSSU Rams facing the Fayetteville State Broncos earlier in the day.
University Police Chief Amir Henry assured the public that the campus was secured. He noted that it was typically a time for the university’s community to come together in “shared pride and connection.”
“Tragically, this year, this celebration has been overshadowed by the loss of life and the injuries resulting from two separate shootings on our campus,” Henry said.
Emergency services audio obtained by NBC News showed officers reporting one victim sustained a gunshot wound to the head. Another recording showed an officer calling for a second ambulance.
Remaining homecoming activities scheduled for Sunday were canceled, including an event at Emmanuel Baptist Church, university Chancellor Bonita J. Brown said in a statement.
Brown expressed her condolences to the family of the deceased victim and said she was praying for the recovery of those who were injured. She also acknowledged that members of the campus community “may have witnessed or experienced things that no one should have to endure.”
She urged people to use the university’s counseling services and continue to follow police instructions as the investigation continues.
“Throughout our history, Winston-Salem State University has faced challenges, but we have always found strength in one another,” Brown wrote. “That is what it means to be part of the Ramily and to be Ram strong.”

sources.news_title: One Dead, 3 Injured in Winston-Salem State University Shootings
sources.text:
One person was killed and three others wounded in shootings on Winston-Salem State University’s campus Saturday night shortly before 10 p.m.
WXII reported that police received a call about a shooting at 9:45 p.m. They discovered there were actually two different shootings but details of either one have yet to be released.
WBAL-TV noted the institution was placed on lockdown then “police allowed students to walk to their dorms on campus” at 1:25 a.m. Sunday. The condition of the three wounded individuals has not been released.
HBCU Gameday pointed out that shootings occurred on Winston-Salem State University’s homecoming weekend, which featured “a football matchup against rival Fayetteville State University at Bowman Gray Stadium.”
Police have not said whether the person or persons responsible for the shooting have ties to the school nor have they said anything to identify the deceased or wounded persons.

sources.text:
WINSTON-SALEM, N.C. (WXII) - One person has died, and three others were injured following two separate shootings at Winston-Salem State University during homecoming on Saturday night.
The Winston-Salem Police Department and the Forsyth County Sheriff's Office held a media briefing at 1:45 a.m. on Sunday on Winston-Salem State's campus.
Other WRAL Top Stories
Winston-Salem police said they received a call around 9:45 p.m. Saturday about a shooting, and the Forsyth County Sheriff's Office confirmed that three people were injured.
The campus was placed on lockdown, but as of 1:25 a.m. Sunday, police were allowing students to walk back to their dorms on campus.
Police are still investigating this incident, and there have been no arrests made at this time. There will be an increase in law enforcement presence on campus in the upcoming days.

2 shootings at Winston-Salem State during homecoming weekend leave 1 dead
sources.text:
Arrest made in deadly shooting during Winston-Salem State homecoming weekend
It is too early to tell whether the shootings were connected, police say.
Authorities on Sunday arrested a man in a shooting during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North Carolina that left one person dead and at least one other person injured.
Winston-Salem police said officers who were on campus for homecoming events heard gunshots around 9:45 p.m. Saturday. They found a 19-year-old man with a gunshot wound. They rendered aid but the man died at the scene.
A 22-year-old woman who had what appeared to be a gunshot wound was taken to a hospital, where she was treated and later released.
Assistant Chief Jason Swaim said at a news conference the investigation led to Ziyaire Spinks, 20, who was arrested and being held without bond on charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon and possession of a firearm on educational property.
According to police, the shooting stemmed from an argument between two groups of people. They confirmed Spinks was not a student at the university.
A second shooting on campus happened less than an hour later, with police responding when they heard shots. In that case, Swaim said two people were injured when gunfire erupted following an altercation.
Authorities said they were investigating to determine if there was any connection between the two shootings. No arrests have been made in the second case.
Chief William Penn, Jr. of the Winston-Salem Police Department vowed during a news conference that authorities will find all of those responsible for the violence at the school.
“It’s important that the blame of these tragic events go to the right people and that’s the folks who committed these acts,” he said, asking people not to point fingers while the investigation is ongoing.
University officials canceled the remainder of homecoming activities Sunday, saying instead that a local church planned to lead a call for prayers in support of the community.
On social media, community members were sharing their condolences and asking for prayers.
Chancellor Bonita J. Brown called the shootings “senseless violence.” In a statement, she assured students, faculty and parents that the campus was secure and that additional law enforcement would remain while the investigation continues.
The school offered counseling for anyone in need.
“We also recognize the concern and anxiety these events have created among our students, parents, families and broader community,” Brown said. “We take our responsibility for campus safety seriously."
Forsyth County Sheriff Bobby Kimbrough, Jr. echoed the sentiments of the chancellor and other law enforcement officials during the news conference.
“Right now, the community is in need of your prayers. The community is in need of us coming together,” Kimbrough said.
___
Montoya Bryan reported from Albuquerque, New Mexico.

sources.news_title: Suspect Arrested After Two Shootings at Winston-Salem State University Leave One Dead, Three Injured
sources.text:
A 20-year-old man faces murder and weapons charges following a fatal shooting during homecoming weekend at the North Carolina university, while investigators examine a second shooting that left two more people wounded.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
WINSTON-SALEM, N.C. — Police arrested a 20-year-old suspect Sunday, Nov. 8, following two shootings at Winston-Salem State University that left a 19-year-old man dead and three other people injured during the historically Black university’s homecoming weekend.
Authorities identified the deceased victim as Peyton Patterson, 19, who was shot Saturday night near South Martin Luther King Jr. Drive. Police arrested Ziyaire Spinks, 20, in connection with Patterson’s death and charged him with murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill or inflict serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on educational property.
According to WXII 12 News’ reporting on the arrest, Spinks was being held without bond as investigators continued examining the circumstances surrounding the violence. Authorities described the fatal shooting as an isolated incident but had not established whether it was connected to a second shooting on campus later that evening.
Officers responding to gunfire shortly after 9:45 p.m. Saturday in the 600 block of South Martin Luther King Jr. Drive discovered Patterson suffering from a gunshot wound. Police and emergency medical personnel attempted lifesaving measures, but he died from his injuries.
A 22-year-old woman was also found wounded at the scene. Emergency responders transported her to a local hospital, where she received treatment before being released.
Approximately 45 minutes later, police responded to another shooting near Victory Circle and Cromartie Street on the university campus.
According to a separate WXII report detailing the second incident, officers arrived shortly before 10:30 p.m. and discovered a 21-year-old man suffering from gunshot injuries. He was transported to a hospital and listed in critical but stable condition.
A 20-year-old woman was also wounded in the second shooting. She was transported to a hospital and reported to be in stable condition.
Investigators located a vehicle believed to be connected to the second incident, but no arrests had been announced in that investigation as of Sunday afternoon.
Police have not identified a motive for either shooting or publicly established whether the incidents involved the same individuals.
The violence prompted university officials to impose an emergency lockdown while officers searched the campus and surrounding areas.
By approximately 1:25 a.m. Sunday, authorities had lifted the lockdown and permitted students to return to their residence halls.
During an early morning news conference, Winston-Salem Police Department Assistant Chief Jason Swaim confirmed that officers were investigating two separate shootings and emphasized that the immediate danger had passed.
“What we can tell you is campus is secure. The surrounding community is secure,” Swaim said, according to NBC News’ coverage of the shootings.
Swaim said investigators were still working to determine what led to the violence and whether the two incidents were connected.
“At this point, the investigation is still very early in its preliminary stages,” he said.
The Winston-Salem Police Department, Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office and university police are cooperating in the investigations.
Authorities announced that additional law enforcement officers would remain on campus Sunday and throughout the coming days to provide security while detectives continue gathering evidence and interviewing witnesses.
The shootings occurred during one of the university’s most heavily attended annual celebrations.
Winston-Salem State had hosted its homecoming football game against Fayetteville State University earlier Saturday, bringing students, graduates, families and other visitors to campus for a weekend of athletic events and reunions.
“Homecoming is traditionally a time of celebration and connection,” Swaim said during the news conference, acknowledging the disruption caused by the violence.
The university subsequently canceled its remaining homecoming activities, including the Fourth Quarter celebration and its scheduled participation in WSSU Day at Emmanuel Baptist Church.
In a statement released Sunday, Chancellor Bonita J. Brown extended condolences to the victim’s family and expressed concern for the injured and those who witnessed the shootings.
“This senseless violence has shaken our university community, and our hearts are heavy,” Brown said.
She acknowledged that students, faculty members and other attendees may have experienced traumatic circumstances during the shootings and emphasized the availability of counseling and support services.
“I recognize that members of our university community may have witnessed or experienced things that no one should have to endure,” Brown said. “I understand the fear, grief and uncertainty that many of you may be feeling. Please know you are not alone.”
The university arranged in-person counseling sessions Sunday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and Monday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. in rooms DJR100 and DJR205. Students were also directed to university counseling services and the Togetherall mental health support platform.
Faculty and staff were offered confidential assistance through the university’s employee assistance program.
Brown said the institution would maintain additional security measures while cooperating with investigators.
“We also recognize the concern and anxiety these events have created among our students, parents, families and broader community,” she said, according to Associated Press reporting. “We take our responsibility for campus safety seriously and remain committed to the well-being of everyone who is part of our university community.”
Winston-Salem State University is a public, historically Black institution within the University of North Carolina system. Founded in 1892, the university serves thousands of undergraduate and graduate students and is an important part of the Winston-Salem community.
The shootings brought an abrupt end to festivities intended to celebrate the school’s history, alumni and student achievements.
Local religious leaders announced plans for a community prayer gathering in response to the violence, while university officials encouraged students and families to monitor official communications for additional safety information.
Investigators have not announced whether Patterson or the three injured victims were enrolled at the university.
Police also have not released information establishing whether the two shootings resulted from personal disputes, involved unrelated suspects or were otherwise connected.
Authorities are asking anyone with information about either incident to contact the Winston-Salem Police Department at 336-773-7700.
As of Sunday afternoon, Spinks remained in custody in connection with the fatal shooting, while investigators continued examining the second incident and gathering evidence.
The university said its campus was secure and that law enforcement personnel would maintain an increased presence as the investigations proceed.

sources.text:
2 charged in deadly shooting at Winston-Salem State during homecoming weekend
A 19-year-old man is dead, a 22-year-old woman was injured, and two men are facing charges after a shooting on the campus of Winston-Salem State University, according to Winston-Salem, North Carolina, police.
“Our condolences go out to the families, to the friends, and anyone who witnessed this,” officials said Sunday.
Video above: Winston-Salem police hold Sunday morning press conference following shooting
Just after 9:45 p.m. Saturday, officers responded to the 600 block of South Martin Luther King Jr. Drive after hearing gunshots in the area.
Police found 19-year-old Peyton Patterson with a gunshot wound and began lifesaving measures. EMS personnel also provided aid, but Patterson died from his injuries.
The circumstances surrounding Patterson's death remain under investigation. Detectives have determined that the shooting was an isolated incident, and Patterson's next of kin has been notified.
22-year-old Alyssa Ellerbee was also found with a gunshot wound. She was taken to a local hospital, where she was treated and released. Police have not released any information about if Ellerbee is a WSSU student at this time.
Police charged 20-year-old Ziyaire Spinks with general murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill or inflict serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on educational property.
18-year-old Cequan Brower was also charged with affray in connection with the incident. Neither of the suspects were students, according to police.
During a news conference, officers said the victims and suspects were in two separate groups when an argument broke out, leading to the shooting that killed Patterson and injured Ellerbee.
Spinks is being held without bond. Brower is being held on a $50,000 bond. Police said both Spinks and Brower will appear in court on Monday. They also have not released their photos at this time due to the investigation being ongoing.
Second shooting happened less than an hour later
Police said the second shooting occurred at 10:22 p.m. on the university's campus. Police said as officers were investigating an earlier incident nearby they also heard gunshots in the area.
Police found 21-year-old Najir Pearsall, who taken to the hospital and was listed in critical but stable condition. Officers said they also located Makyiah Ward, 20, who had been shot and was also taken to the hospital. She was listed in stable condition at this time. Police said they identified and later found a vehicle related to the incident.
Police said the circumstances around the shooting are still under investigation, and no arrests have been made. They also have not said if Pearsall or Ward are students at WSSU.
Chancellor Bonita J. Brown issued a statement Sunday morning, calling the shootings “senseless violence.” She assured students, faculty and parents that the campus was secure and that additional law enforcement would remain while the investigation continues.

sources.news_title: Winston-Salem State University placed on alert over reports of shooting during homecoming weekend
sources.text:
Winston-Salem State University placed on alert over reports of shooting during homecoming weekend
Reports of gunfire and multiple victims prompted safety concerns at the North Carolina HBCU.
Winston-Salem State University (WSSU) in North Carolina was placed under heightened security after reports of a possible shooting during its homecoming party on Saturday. Several social media posts claimed that gunfire broke out on or near the university campus, with reports of multiple victims and a possible lockdown.
The reports emerged during WSSU’s homecoming celebrations, an annual event that attracts students, alumni and visitors to the historically Black university in Winston-Salem, North Carolina.
Students and relatives posted messages online saying some people had been instructed to remain inside their rooms while security officials assessed the situation.
Social media reports of university lockdown and shooting
Social media accounts began circulating claims of a shooting involving multiple victims on campus. Some posts alleged that at least two people had been shot and suggested a possible third victim.
“1 GUN SHOT WOUND TO THE HEAD ON CAMPUS...2 PPL SHOT...POSSIBLE 3r SHOT...THEY ASKING FOR CURTAINS SO IM ASSUMING ITS A DEAD BODY...CHECK ON YA PPL....#WSSUhomecoming,” one Facebook user wrote.
One user on Facebook, a parent of a student at the university, wrote, “Family there was a shooting up at Winston Salem homing coming at a party.”
She added, “Sweet is okay she wasn't at the party and they don't think students was doing the shooting but some people got shot.”
Another user wrote, “RAM-ALERT!! Winston-Salem State University Lockdown Following Reported Residence Hall Shooting Sparks Campus Safety Concerns!”
The user added, “Thank God for always covering my child, she is on lock down in her room safe! Praying for any individuals that may be affected! We have to do better too many incidents especially at what are supposed to positive Homecoming celebrations at HBCUS!”
Another user who was around the area wrote, “We was in that homecoming traffic. Please [Police] presents was really heavy we saw about five high point police cars 2 to 3 surf cars from High Point and the Winston Salem presents. We was in traffic for abt 30 mins or longer. So sumbdy got shot in da head doing homecoming.”
Another post claimed the incident occurred during a homecoming event and that multiple fights followed the reported shooting. However, no official law enforcement agency had confirmed those claims at the time of publication.
Authorities expected to provide further updates
Law enforcement agencies and university officials were expected to release more information as they investigated the reports.
Emergency response teams typically secure the scene, identify potential suspects and determine whether there is any ongoing threat before releasing details to the public.
The university, located in Winston-Salem, is one of the nation’s historically Black universities and has an enrolment of thousands of students. It is known for its homecoming celebrations, which bring together current students, alumni and community members each year.
At the time of writing, students and families are expecting for confirmed information about the reported shooting and any possible injuries.

sources.news_title: HBCU on-campus shooting leaves one dead, three shot following homecoming
sources.text:
WINSTON-SALEM, N.C. — One person is dead and three others were shot following two separate shooting incidents on the campus of HBCU Winston-Salem State University Saturday night, according to the Winston-Salem Police Department.
The deadly violence occurred during the university’s homecoming weekend, a major annual celebration that brings alumni, students and supporters back to campus.
WXII 12 News reported early Sunday morning that Winston-Salem police confirmed one person had died and three others were shot during the incidents.
The television station updated its reporting at 3:24 a.m. Sunday, November 8, confirming the fatality.
Winston-Salem State shooting leaves one dead
Police initially confirmed receiving a call about a shooting on the Winston-Salem State campus around 9:45 p.m. Saturday, November 7.
Forsyth County Emergency Medical Services confirmed that three shooting victims were transported to a hospital. Authorities subsequently confirmed that one person was dead following two separate shooting incidents on campus.
The conditions of the three additional victims have not been publicly disclosed. Police have not released the identity of the deceased individual or indicated whether any of the victims were students at Winston-Salem State.
Additional details about where the shootings occurred on campus, what led to the violence and whether the incidents were connected have not been confirmed.
Information about potential suspects or arrests was also not immediately available.
Deadly violence strikes HBCU during homecoming
The shooting occurred during one of the most significant weekends on the Winston-Salem State calendar.
The historic HBCU hosted its annual homecoming celebration Saturday, including a football matchup against rival Fayetteville State University at Bowman Gray Stadium.
Homecoming traditionally draws thousands of alumni, students, families and supporters to Winston-Salem for a weekend of reunions, celebrations and university-sponsored activities.
The deadly incidents cast a shadow over the festivities.
Winston-Salem State, founded in 1892, is a public HBCU and member of the University of North Carolina System. The university has been a cornerstone of the Winston-Salem community for more than 130 years.
The shootings also raise renewed concerns about campus safety and security during large gatherings that attract visitors from beyond the university community.
Investigation continues at Winston-Salem State
The Winston-Salem Police Department continues investigating the circumstances surrounding the two shootings.
As of early Sunday morning, authorities had not publicly identified the deceased person or the three other victims.
Questions also remain about whether the incidents involved members of the university community and whether either shooting was connected to official homecoming activities.
The confirmation of one person dead and three others injured represents a tragic turn for a weekend intended to bring the Winston-Salem State community together.
HBCU Gameday will continue monitoring the investigation and provide updates as additional information becomes available.
This is a developing story. Information is based on reporting by WXII 12 News, which cited the Winston-Salem Police Department and Forsyth County Emergency Medical Services.
